---
title: "Responsible AI for Official Statistics"
subtitle: "The Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Official Statistics"
---

## About the Training

The aim of this training is to present the principles of responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in official statistics.

The materials cover ethical, methodological, technological and organisational aspects of using AI at different stages of the statistical process.

The training demonstrates how to make use of the opportunities offered by artificial intelligence while taking into account the limitations of AI models, data protection, the quality of results and accountability for decisions made.

## Training Programme

### 1. Introduction to the Responsible Use of AI

An introduction to the concept of responsible artificial intelligence, its importance in official statistics, and the fundamental principles of safe and reliable use of AI.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R01.qmd)

### 2. Fundamentals of AI and Machine Learning

Key concepts related to artificial intelligence, machine learning and generative models. An overview of common applications of AI in statistical data analysis and the limitations of different methods.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R02.qmd)

### 3. Data Confidentiality and Security

Principles of safe data use in AI systems, protection of confidential information, data minimisation, and risks associated with using external tools.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R03.qmd)

### 4. Algorithmic Bias and Fairness

Sources of bias in data and models, the risk of unequal performance across different groups, and methods for assessing and mitigating undesirable differences in AI model performance.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R04.qmd)

### 5. Transparency and Documentation

Documentation of data, methods, models, validation results and limitations. Explainability of AI outputs and ensuring that the solutions used can be reproduced and verified.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R05.qmd)

### 6. Oversight and Accountability

Roles and responsibilities in AI projects, human oversight of model outputs, and principles for intervention, approval and withdrawal of AI solutions.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R06.qmd)

### 7. AI in the GSBPM Statistical Process

Opportunities for using AI at different stages of the statistical process — from identifying needs and designing surveys to data processing, analysis, dissemination of results and evaluation.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R07.qmd)

### 8. Generative AI in Official Statistics

Practical applications of generative models and large language models (LLMs), prompt engineering, the use of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and verification of AI-generated content and code.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R08.qmd)

### 9. Validation and Monitoring of AI Systems

Assessment of model quality before and after deployment, selection of evaluation metrics, comparison with baseline methods, detection of changes in data, and principles of revalidation.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R09.qmd)

### 10. AI Governance in Organisations

Principles for managing AI applications within an organisation, AI system registers, risk assessment, procedures for deploying and withdrawing systems, and developing employees' skills and competencies.

[Go to chapter](chapters/R10.qmd)

## Summary

The responsible use of AI in official statistics requires combining statistical and technological expertise with appropriate oversight, data protection, transparency and systematic quality assessment.

The goal is not simply to implement new technologies, but to use them consciously wherever they can improve the quality, efficiency and reliability of the statistical process.
